Interface Display

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractDisplay, MacDisplay, UnixDisplay, WindowsDisplay
@PublicApi @Immutable public interface Display
Display refers to the information regarding a video source and monitor identified by the EDID standard.

getDisplayInfo() returns a DisplayInfo exposing the display's decoded attributes — manufacturer ID, product ID, serial number, physical dimensions, preferred resolution, model name, and the raw (or synthesized) EDID byte array.

Example: extracting monitor manufacturer and dimensions: 

for (Display display : hal.getDisplays()) {
    DisplayInfo info = display.getDisplayInfo();
    System.out.println("Manufacturer: " + info.getManufacturerID());
    System.out.println("Product ID:   " + info.getProductID());
    System.out.printf("Size: %d cm x %d cm%n", info.getHcm(), info.getVcm());
}
For displays that report their attributes without providing an EDID (such as a built-in macOS Retina panel), DisplayInfo.isEdidSynthetic() returns true and DisplayInfo.getEdid() returns an EDID synthesized from those attributes.

What the display is, as described by its EDID, is on DisplayInfo. How it is attached and how the windowing system is currently driving it, such as getDevicePort() and getCurrentMode(), is on this interface.

    • getDevicePort

      default String getDevicePort()
      The system-level device identification for this display. The form of the identifier is platform-specific:
      • Linux: the DRM connector name from sysfs (e.g. HDMI-A-1, eDP-1, DP-2), or the xrandr output name when DRM sysfs is not available.
      • macOS: on Apple Silicon, the port named by an external monitor's framebuffer TransportDescription (e.g. Port-HDMI@1, Port-USB-C@1), or the built-in panel's device tree name (e.g. disp0). Intel Macs do not expose a port.
      • Windows: the connector derived from the Connecting and Configuring Displays (CCD) API's output technology and connector instance (e.g. HDMI, DisplayPort-1).
      • Other UNIX platforms: the xrandr output name, which is the same value getOutputName() returns.
      Returns:
      The device port identifier, or Constants.UNKNOWN if not available.

    • getOutputName

      default Optional<String> getOutputName()
      The X11 output name for this display as reported by xrandr (e.g. HDMI-1, DP2). This is the name to pass to xrandr --output. Implemented on Linux and the other UNIX platforms, and only available where an X server with the RandR extension is reachable. On Linux the display is matched to an X output by its DRM CONNECTOR_ID, falling back to a comparison of their EDIDs.
      Returns:
      An Optional containing the xrandr output name, or empty if not available.

    • getCurrentMode

      default Optional<DisplayMode> getCurrentMode()
      The mode the windowing system is currently driving this display in: its size, pixel resolution, refresh rate, rotation, and position on the desktop.

      The display must be matched to the windowing system's own view of it, which is done lazily on the first call:

      • macOS: by comparing the EDID's vendor, product and serial numbers with those CoreGraphics reports. Two connected monitors that report identical numbers cannot be told apart, and neither returns a mode.
      • Windows: by the monitor's device path, through the Connecting and Configuring Displays (CCD) API.
      • Linux and the other UNIX platforms: by the xrandr output that getOutputName() names, so an X server with the RandR extension must be reachable.
      A Display is a snapshot, so the mode is read once and not refreshed; query the displays again to see a change.
      Returns:
      An Optional containing the current mode, or empty if the display is not active on the desktop or cannot be matched to the windowing system.

    • isBuiltIn

      default Optional<Boolean> isBuiltIn()
      Whether this display is built into the device, such as a laptop panel, rather than an external monitor.
      • macOS: CoreGraphics' own classification for a display it can match, and known directly for the Apple Silicon built-in panel and external ports.
      • Windows: from the output technology the CCD API reports for the display's connector, where embedded DisplayPort, LVDS, embedded UDI and internal connections are built in.
      • Linux and the other UNIX platforms: from the connector name, where eDP, LVDS and DSI connectors are built in.
      Returns:
      An Optional containing true if the display is built in, false if it is external, or empty if it cannot be determined.

    • isPrimary

      default Optional<Boolean> isPrimary()
      Whether this display is the primary display: the one the windowing system treats as the main desktop, placing it at the desktop origin and, on macOS, giving it the menu bar.

      As for getCurrentMode(), the display must be matched to the windowing system's own view of it, which is done lazily on the first call:

      • macOS: CoreGraphics' main display, as CGDisplayIsMain reports it. A display is matched by comparing the EDID's vendor, product and serial numbers with those CoreGraphics reports, and the Apple Silicon built-in panel by its built-in flag. Two active monitors that report identical numbers cannot be told apart, and neither returns a value; if CoreGraphics lists only one of them as active, both are matched to it and report its status.
      • Windows: the display whose desktop position in its current mode is the origin, which is how Windows defines the primary display. A display that is attached but not active on the desktop has no current mode, and returns no value.
      • Linux and the other UNIX platforms: the xrandr output marked primary, matched as getOutputName() describes, so an X server with the RandR extension must be reachable. Under Wayland without an X server, or on a headless system, no value is returned.
      Exactly one display reporting true is not guaranteed. On Windows, a display cloning the primary display shares its desktop position and also reports true. X11 need not designate a primary output at all, in which case every output reports false.

      A Display is a snapshot, so the status is read once and not refreshed; query the displays again to see a change.

      Returns:
      An Optional containing true if the display is the primary display, false if it is not, or empty if it cannot be determined because the display cannot be matched to the windowing system.
